doc.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier and Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-01-18

title: Playing rags and show-band snare beats; Red Happy Bolton
summary: Williams says beats are varied accordingly for rags. He recalls buck-and-wing dancing on old shows and show-band drummers' snare beats, including Red Happy Bolton at the Lyric Theatre.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How about when you would be playing the rags, you know, you would play maybe some rags in them days, would you keep all on snare drums playing some?

Yeah, same, that's how we'd change the beats, like I tell you, the variety of beats, just change them accordingly, that's all I could explain, you know what I mean, whatever you're playing. But that's how we played all the, there was the same drag that he was doing just now. Yeah. Now, see, some drummers might do this, you see, like he'd be playing, like, dun, dun, dun, dun. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. I used to do a buck and wing dance, tap dance, you know, buck dance years ago on the old shows. When he'd be followed the band, he'd snag them all the way through the band. Well, all right, now, while he'd be doing that for that band, same time, any particular number, the John Rocha band, he'd have that same snag drum beat. Yeah, that's that. With the band, all the way through the dance number. I mean, with the show band, that was his snare drum beat. And some of them, I'd sometimes put those numbers myself. Sometimes I'd be doing that, or sometimes I'd get... I mean, with that, all them fellas did that, a year ago. Yeah, they put all that down, you know, and some fast numbers they'd be playing. Was that Red Happy you were talking about? Red Happy, yeah, that's Red Happy, yeah. Lyrite Theatre? Lyrite Theatre, right out here on Burgundy and I. Is it Happy Bolton? Is it Happy Bolton? You know, I've never been to know Happy Bolton.
I think that's his name is Bolton.
